entries.title: Job 29:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Preserved - From all those miseries which now I feel.

entries.title: Job 29:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Darkness - I passed safely through many difficulties, and dangers, and common calamities.

entries.title: Job 29:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Seat - When I caused the seat of justice to be set for me. By this, and several other expressions, it appears that Job was a magistrate. Street - In that open place, near the gate, where the people assembled for the administration of justice.

entries.title: Job 29:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Cleaved - It lay as still as if he had done so.

entries.title: Job 29:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Witness - Gave testimony to my pious, and just, and blameless conversation.

entries.title: Job 29:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Put on, &100. - Perhaps he did not wear these: but his steady justice was to him instead of all those ornaments.

entries.title: Job 29:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Multiply - See how apt even good men are, to set death at a distance from them!

entries.title: Job 29:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Glory - My reputation was growing every day. Bow - My strength which is signified by a bow, Gen 49:24 1Sam 2:4, because in ancient times the bow and arrows were the principal instruments of war.

entries.title: Job 29:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Dropped - As the rain, which when it comes down gently upon the earth, is most acceptable and beneficial to it.

entries.title: Job 29:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Laughed - Carried myself so familiarly with them, that they could scarce believe their eyes and ears. Cast not down - They were cautious not to give me any occasion to change my countenance towards them.

entries.title: Job 29:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I chose - They sought to me for advice in all difficult cases, and I directed them what methods they should take. Sat - As a prince or judge, while they stood waiting for my counsel. A king - Whose presence puts life, and courage, into the whole army. As one - As I was ready to comfort any afflicted persons, so my consolations were always welcome to them.
